sso.loginsEmpty: Nobody has signed in through this provider yet.

mapping.body: Each sign-in reads the {{claim}} claim and applies the first rule that matches for each target. With no role rule matching, the account is a {{role}}.
mapping.rules: Only what these rules created is changed at sign-in. A membership or role an administrator set by hand wins, and the user page marks a role that differs.

channelBody.saml: Signed assertions posted to the console — what Identity Center offers custom apps.
channelBody.oidc: Authorization code + PKCE — what most open-source IdPs speak.

sso.claimsBodySaml: The SAML attribute each value is read from — the exact Name the IdP sends (URIs allowed). The NameID is the account's subject; an emailAddress NameID also serves as the email.

saml.rotateHint: A new SP key and certificate — import the console's metadata at the IdP again afterwards
saml.rotated: A new SP key is in place — import the metadata at the IdP again
saml.uploadHint: The XML your IdP lets you download
saml.awaiting: Nothing received yet: load the IdP's metadata, or enter its entity ID, SSO URL and certificate under Connection.
saml.sloHint: When set, signing out also ends the IdP session (HTTP-Redirect binding).
saml.certsHint: PEM, one per block; two while the IdP rotates its key.
saml.idpInitiatedBody: Users can start from the IdP's portal (the Identity Center app tile). Off: only from the console.
saml.signRequestsBody: Sign AuthnRequests and LogoutRequests with the SP key — for IdPs that require it (Keycloak's default).
saml.wantEncryptedBody: Refuse an assertion that is not encrypted to the SP certificate.
saml.encryptedIcNote: Identity Center does not encrypt assertions for custom applications by default — sign-in will be refused unless it does.

body.default: Your IdP pushes accounts and group membership here ahead of sign-in: a deactivated user loses access at once, and group membership drives the same mappings a sign-in applies.
body.identity-center: IAM Identity Center provisions inbound only: it does not push users to custom SAML applications. Map groups through the groups attribute, or use SCIM from an IdP that offers it (Entra ID, Okta, Authentik).

scim.once: Shown once — copy it into your IdP now

scim.revokeBody: The token stops working at once. What SCIM has provisioned — accounts and groups — stays.
scim.subject: Subject
scim.subjectHint: The SCIM attribute that equals the NameID / sub this IdP signs users in with — userName for most.

stdio.label: Transport
stdio.on: stdio server — run it behind the platform's streamable-HTTP bridge
stdio.hint: For a server that only speaks stdio. The deploy adds the bridge (samples/mcp_stdio_bridge/), which serves 0.0.0.0:8000/mcp and starts your command as its subprocess. Leave off when the server already serves streamable HTTP.
stdio.zipOnly: The bridge wraps code zips only. For a Dockerfile context or an image, build the bridge in yourself from samples/mcp_stdio_bridge/.

baseHint.python: Runs on the managed Python runtime; requirements.txt is resolved as usual. python / python3 is the runtime's interpreter.
baseHint.node: Builds an image on the bridge's Node 22 base (CodeBuild, arm64; npm ci --omit=dev) and deploys it as a container. Ship built JavaScript; a Dockerfile in the zip is replaced.

stdio.commandHint: The program only, e.g. python, node or npx. It runs from the zip root without a shell.
stdio.argsHint: One per line, passed exactly as written (at most {{max}}).
stdio.errCommand: One word, no spaces — put the rest in Arguments.
stdio.errArgs: At most {{max}} arguments of up to 1024 characters each.
stdio.limits: One server process per container: fine for a stateless server or a single session. A server that keeps per-session state sees every caller as one session. Responses are plain JSON — the server's progress and logging notifications are dropped, and requests it sends back (sampling, elicitation, roots) are answered as unsupported.

mount.note: Managed session storage persists files under its mount path across stop/resume of the same session (14-day idle expiry); every re-publish resets it. S3 Files / EFS mounts are shared across sessions and need the agent in a VPC network profile.
mount.noteByo: S3 Files / EFS mounts run in the agent's VPC network profile (TCP 2049 egress to the mount targets required). The execution role is granted mount permissions automatically, and the agent is told the mounted paths. Re-publish resets managed session storage only.
mount.adminOnly: S3 Files / EFS mounts are set by an administrator. You can re-publish with them or remove them; ask an administrator to add or change one.
mount.askAdmin: Need a shared S3 Files / EFS directory? An administrator can add the mount.
mount.needsProfile: S3 Files / EFS mounts need the agent in a VPC — choose a network profile in the network step.

mcp.public: Public (AgentCore managed network). Choose a VPC profile in the network step when the server's tools call private back ends (databases, internal APIs).
mcp.vpc: VPC profile {{id}}: the server's outbound calls leave from the profile's subnets. The Gateway still reaches it through the AgentCore data plane, not through your VPC. The profile needs the endpoints for pulling the image and for the server's own back ends; bedrock-runtime is usually not needed.

header.label: Where this page is on the storyline

turn.title: Your turn
turn.none: Nothing waits on you right now.

goldenStandard.name: Golden standard
goldenStandard.short: The golden test set plus the five-dimension criteria (cognition, quality, responsibility, cost, performance). All six stages turn around it: Define produces it, Evaluate draws on it, Release decides by it, Improve feeds production failures back into it.

drillDown.name: Three-level drill-down (session / trajectory / step)
drillDown.short: When a case fails, locate it level by level: the session shows whether the whole turn failed, the trajectory pins the step that went wrong, the step shows what exactly it did.

criteria.name: Criterion
criteria.short: One checkable quality rule, such as "never promise a refund outside the policy".

criteriaSet.name: Criteria table
criteriaSet.short: An agent's criteria as one versioned table: frozen when published, then signed by someone other than its editor.

criteriaTier.name: Red line / gate / observe
criteriaTier.short: Criteria come in three tiers: a red line vetoes on contact, a gate must be met to release, an observe criterion only watches until its calibration proves it, then moves up.

goldenSet.name: Golden set
goldenSet.short: The scenarios the agent is measured on, tied to one criteria table.

goldenSplit.name: Dev / regression / holdout
goldenSplit.short: The golden set's three splits: dev to iterate on, regression to replay, holdout written once and sealed for the gate.

caseTier.name: Case tier
caseTier.short: How hard or important a scenario is, so coverage shows where the set is thin.

admission.name: Sample admission
admission.short: Improve's "admit into the set": after attribution clustering, a person decides which production samples join the golden set; once in, a sample is part of the standard.

judgeCalibration.name: Judge calibration
judgeCalibration.short: Comparing an LLM judge with human labels; an uncalibrated judge cannot hold a gate.

gate.name: Release gate
gate.short: Runs the candidate against the criteria and says PASS, BLOCKED or INVALID, criterion by criterion.

passK.name: pass^k
passK.short: A scenario passes only if it passes k runs in a row — for behaviour that must be reliable, not lucky.

waiver.name: Waiver
waiver.short: A time-limited exception for one blocked gate criterion, with a risk owner and a compensating control. Red lines are never waived.

releaseRecord.name: Decision record
releaseRecord.short: Who released, blocked or rolled back which version, on what evidence — the audit trail.

driftWatch.name: Drift watch
driftWatch.short: Keeps measuring the live version against its criteria and raises an alert when it slips.

repairLadder.name: Fix ladder
repairLadder.short: One change per rung, each rerun on the same yardstick, so every gain is attributable to that one change (F1–F5 in the methodology).

scorecard.name: Scorecard
scorecard.short: An agent's standard on one page: last gate, criteria, coverage, open waivers and alerts.

group.basicsWhen: Name, instructions, protocol and model — every agent needs these.
group.toolsWhen: What the agent can do beyond answering: built-in tools, Gateway, Identity, Skills and knowledge.
group.behaviourWhen: Tune how the model answers: sampling, thinking, caching and prompt templates.
group.outputWhen: How much history the agent keeps, and whether it also returns a structured answer.
group.advancedWhen: Inbound auth and file storage — leave as is unless you know you need them.

tools.label: Strands built-in tools
tools.hint: Curated from strands-agents-tools. None picked: the agent keeps the template's calculator and current_utc_time.
tools.replaceNote: Picked tools replace the template's calculator and current_utc_time.
tools.sandboxNote: shell, python_repl, file_write and use_aws run only in a sandbox — see Sandboxed tools below.
tools.retrieveNoKb: Mount a knowledge base below first — retrieve searches the agent's own.
tools.retrieveA2a: A2A agents carry no knowledge base, so retrieve is not available.
tools.hostsHint: Host names only, comma separated; *.example.com covers its subdomains. Redirects are not followed.
tools.hostsNone: No host — the tool would reach nothing, so it is refused

when.current_time: Questions about today, deadlines or time zones.
when.calculator: Exact arithmetic, algebra and unit math instead of guessing.
when.http_request: Call a public or partner API on hosts you allow.
when.think: Hard, multi-step problems that benefit from a few reflection passes.
when.retrieve: Pull passages from a mounted knowledge base by query.
when.image_reader: Read an image file the agent was given and describe it.
when.journal: Keep running notes or a task log across turns of a session.

params.title: Inference parameters
params.sub: Blank = the model's own default. Part of the config bundle, so an experiment can compare them.
params.temperatureWhen: Lower for consistent, factual answers; higher for varied wording.
params.topPWhen: An alternative to temperature — Claude takes one of the two.
params.maxTokensWhen: Cap a single reply; raise it for long reports.
params.stopWhen: One per line, up to 4 — the model stops when it writes one.
params.mantleNote: Stop sequences, extended thinking and prompt caching are Bedrock Converse options — not available on Bedrock Mantle.
params.thinkingWhen: Claude reasons step by step before answering — better on hard problems, slower and costlier.
params.thinkingClaudeOnly: Claude models only — pick a Claude model in Basics to use it.
params.cachingWhen: Long system prompt or many tools, many turns: cached prefix cuts cost and latency.
params.budgetWhen: At least 1024. The reply gets room on top of this budget.

prompt.title: Prompt template
prompt.sub: Variables and examples are applied to the system prompt on every request; a config bundle can still override the prompt.
prompt.variablesWhen: Write {{ph}} in the instructions to fill it per request: the call's context first, then the runtime env, then the default here.
prompt.fewShotWhen: Show a few question / answer pairs when the answer's format or tone matters.
prompt.question: Question

output.title: Conversation & structured output
output.sub: How the conversation is trimmed as it grows, and an optional structured answer.

when.default: What every agent gets today: the last 40 messages are kept.
when.sliding_window: Short tasks or tight budgets: keep only the most recent messages.
when.summarizing: Long sessions where early details still matter: older turns are summarised, recent ones kept.

output.windowWhen: 2 – 1000. Fewer messages, fewer tokens per turn.
output.summaryModelWhen: A cheaper Bedrock model for the summaries; blank uses the agent's model.
output.schemaWhen: When a program reads the answer: /v1 returns it as `structured` next to the text answer.
output.schemaA2a: A2A agents answer in A2A message parts — structured output is not available.

err.httpHosts: Add at least one allowed host. {{detail}}
err.retrieve: retrieve needs a mounted knowledge base.
err.topP: Top P must be between 0 and 1.
err.maxTokens: Max output tokens must be a whole number from 1 to 131072.
err.stopSequences: Up to 4 stop sequences, each at most 100 characters.
err.thinkingBudget: The thinking budget must be a whole number from 1024 to 131072.
err.thinkingTemperature: Extended thinking cannot be combined with a temperature — clear it.
err.thinkingTopP: Extended thinking needs Top P of at least 0.95 (or none).
err.thinkingMaxTokens: Max output tokens must be larger than the thinking budget.
err.claudeBoth: Claude models take temperature or Top P, not both — clear one of them.
err.windowSize: Messages kept must be a whole number from 2 to 1000.
err.outputSchemaA2a: A2A agents cannot return structured output — clear the schema.
err.outputSchemaGuardrail: Structured output cannot be combined with PII protection yet.
err.variables: Variable names start with a letter or _ and are unique (at most 20). {{detail}}
err.fewShot: Every example needs both a question and an answer (at most 10).
err.agentToolName: Tool names start with a letter, then letters, digits or _ (at most 64): {{detail}}
err.agentToolDuplicate: Tool name {{detail}} is already used — rename it.
err.agentToolDescription: Describe when to call each agent (at most 1000 characters).
err.agentToolCount: At most {{detail}} agents can be offered as tools.
err.providerConnection: Pick the API key Connection that holds the provider's key.
err.providerBaseUrl: Enter the gateway's http(s) address — no credentials, query or fragment. {{detail}}
err.providerConverse: Extended thinking and prompt caching are Bedrock options — turn them off for this provider.
err.approvalTools: Approval entries are tool names or * patterns: {{detail}}
err.maxToolCalls: Tool calls per turn must be a whole number from 1 to 500.
err.maskArgs: Masked arguments are names of letters, digits, _ . or -: {{detail}}
err.retryAttempts: Attempts must be a whole number from 1 to 10.
err.retryInitial: The first delay must be 1 to 60 seconds.
err.retryMax: The ceiling must be 1 to 600 seconds and at least the first delay.
err.customToolName: Tool names start with a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits or _ (at most 64). {{detail}}
err.customToolDuplicate: {{detail}} is already a tool of this agent — rename it.
err.customToolDescription: Say when to call the tool (at most 1000 characters).
err.customToolCode: Write the tool's code (at most 20000 characters).
err.customToolRequirement: Pin each requirement as name==version, at most 10. {{detail}}
err.customToolSandboxRequirements: A tool that runs in the Code Interpreter cannot declare requirements.

agents.label: Other agents as tools
agents.hint: Deployed agents of this project the model can hand a sub-task to. Use it when another agent already owns a domain — billing, a policy desk, a research assistant.
agents.none: No other deployed agent can be called
agents.descriptionPlaceholder: Say what this agent knows and when to ask it — the model reads this to decide.
agents.blocked: {{count}} agents of this project cannot be called

block.self: This is the agent being edited.
block.not_runtime: A managed Harness agent cannot be called as a tool yet.
block.protocol: An MCP server — attach it as a tool instead.
block.jwt_inbound: Accepts JWT bearer tokens only; this agent signs with IAM.

agents.roleNote: Calls run with this agent's own execution role; the platform grants invoke on exactly these runtimes. Sub-agents of an agent stop at depth 3.

guards.label: Tool-call guards
guards.hint: Hooks around every tool call: pause for a person, cap the calls, keep a masked log.
guards.approvalWhen: Tools with side effects (send, pay, delete). The console chat shows an approval card; /v1, evaluations and other agents get a clear refusal instead.
guards.capWhen: Stops a looping agent; the next call is refused and the model told to answer.
guards.logWhen: One line per call in the runtime log group: name, status, duration and arguments.
guards.maskWhen: Argument names shown as *** in the log and on the approval card — password, secret, token, api_key and authorization always are.

provider.label: Model provider

when.bedrock: The model from Basics, through Bedrock with this agent's role — no key needed.
when.anthropic: Call Claude on the Anthropic API directly, with your organisation's API key.
when.litellm: Route through your company's LiteLLM gateway — one entry point, its own keys and budgets.

provider.noKeys: No API key Connection yet — create one under Identity → Connections, then pick it here.

baseUrlWhen.anthropic: Optional — only for a proxy in front of the Anthropic API.

provider.modelNote: The key is read from the token vault at run time and never stored in the agent's spec. Set the model in Basics to the provider's model name (a custom model id).
provider.notHere: A model provider applies to HTTP agents on Bedrock only — this agent keeps its Bedrock model.

retry.label: Custom throttling retry
retry.default: Off: the SDK default — 6 attempts, 4 s doubling to 240 s.
retry.when: When the model throttles, wait and try again; the delay doubles up to the ceiling.
retry.ladder: Waits at most {{total}} s in all before the turn fails.
retry.noRetry: One attempt — a throttled call fails at once.

sandbox.label: Sandboxed tools
sandbox.hint: The high-risk built-in tools. Each call runs in an AgentCore Code Interpreter session — never in this agent's runtime, with its role, files or memory.
sandbox.open: Opened in this workspace by an administrator.
sandbox.closed: Closed in this workspace — an administrator opens them below or in the workspace's sandbox setting.
sandbox.closedPick: {{tools}} is no longer allowed in this workspace — remove it, or ask an administrator to open it; the deploy refuses it.

when.python_repl: Data wrangling and calculations by running Python; variables persist across calls.
when.shell: Command-line utilities, in the sandbox's own machine.
when.file_write: Write a file python_repl and shell then work on.
when.use_aws: Call AWS APIs with the sandbox's role (a custom Code Interpreter with an execution role).

sandbox.interpreterHint: Empty = the AWS-managed aws.codeinterpreter.v1 (no AWS credentials). use_aws needs a custom interpreter with an execution role.
sandbox.saveNote: Applies to every agent of this workspace at its next deploy.

custom.label: Custom Python tools
custom.hint: Your own @tool functions, packaged with the agent. The code is checked as you type; anything outside the allow-list needs an administrator's approval of that exact version.
custom.addWhen: When no built-in tool does the job — a calculation, a parser, a call to your own service.
custom.name: Tool name

runsWhen.runtime: Imported from the zip; it runs with the agent's role and can use its declared requirements.
runsWhen.code_interpreter: Each call runs in a sandbox session; the agent's runtime never imports the code. Preinstalled packages only.

custom.descriptionPlaceholder: What the tool does and when the model should call it.
custom.requirementsHint: One name==version per line. Every requirement is reviewed with the tool.
custom.requirementsSandbox: The sandbox installs nothing — leave this empty.

verdict.idle: Waiting for a name and code to check.
verdict.review_one: {{count}} finding — this version deploys once an administrator approves it.
verdict.review_other: {{count}} findings — this version deploys once an administrator approves it.
verdict.approved: Approved by {{who}} on {{when}} — any change to the code needs a new approval.

custom.notePlaceholder: Why this is safe (optional, kept with the approval)
custom.askAdmin: Ask an administrator to review and approve this version — the deploy refuses it until then.
